title: CasperProver — equivocation & double-signing battery
description: Fixtures for detecting agent equivocation: same agent produces two conflicting proofs for the same (model, input) pair. This is the ZK/multi-agent analog of double-spend / slashing offense. See stake-slashing contract for the on-chain enforcement.
target_flow: POST /inference/prove twice with same (agent, model_id, input) but different `output`
invariants: Two proofs from the same agent for the same (model, input) with different outputs MUST be detectable as equivocation.
The equivocation detector MUST be deterministic — same pair of proofs always classified the same way.
Anchored proofs (with deploy_hash) MUST allow slashing via stake-slashing contract when equivocation is proven on-chain.
The detector MUST NOT flag benign non-determinism (different model_id, different input, different agent).

expect.reason: different agents may legitimately disagree — that's the point of multi-agent quorum
different models are allowed to produce different answers
we hash bytes, not semantics — any byte-level diff = potential equivocation; agent must sign canonical form
byte-level diff — canonicalization is the agent's responsibility, not the verifier's

expected_flow: 1. Two conflicting proofs (proof_a.deploy_hash, proof_b.deploy_hash) submitted via /verify
2. Verifier confirms same (agent, model, input) but different output
3. slash_equivocation(proof_a_id, proof_b_id) called by any observer
4. Contract validates both proofs exist and conflict, deducts agent's stake, emits SlashedEvent
5. Slashed dict marks the (agent, model, input) tuple as burned — no re-slash possible
